thesis: Most AI coding assistant pilots don't fail on model quality; they stall around day 90 because the organisation measured seat activation instead of changed work, so the renewal decision arrives with no evidence either way.

anecdotes.summary: Opening scene: CFO asks what changed, 92% activation slide; callback in close.

claims.statement: Halvorsen Research interviewed platform teams at 32 companies for its May 2026 report, "Platform teams and AI tooling." The median pilot in that group ran 94 days before a renewal decision.
The Northfield Developer Survey 2026 asked 1,240 developers in March 2026 about their company's assistant pilot. 61% said the pilot had "no agreed success measure" at launch.
Among pilots with no success measure, weekly active use fell from 78% in month one to 41% by month three. Among pilots that had one, it fell from 80% to 66%.
By month three the pilots without a measure were at 41% weekly active use against 66% for pilots with one.
The point where weekly use has slid furthest in unmeasured pilots is about when the median pilot in Halvorsen's group faces its renewal call.
Of the 32 companies, 9 tracked any change in cycle time or review load during the pilot. All 9 renewed. Of the 23 that tracked only seat activation, 11 renewed.
11 of 23 companies renewed with nothing but activation data; fewer than half of them survived.
9 is a small group, and 9 out of 9 is a result that invites overreading.
Halvorsen's data come from interviews with 32 companies, not a controlled trial.
When the CFO asks what changed, those 9 companies had something to show. The other 23 had a usage chart.
Halvorsen counted companies that tracked any change in cycle time or review load.
A November 2025 Ostrava University study, "Assistant use and review latency," looked at 400 pull requests and found no measurable change in review time with assistant use.
It should change how you read Halvorsen's 9 out of 9.
It's one study of 400 pull requests, and review time is one measure among several.
Halvorsen counted any change in cycle time or review load. Pick the one your code review tool already records.
The median pilot in Halvorsen's group ran 94 days.
Northfield's month-three numbers, 41% for pilots with no success measure and 66% for pilots with one, are the drop to watch for.
Given Ostrava's finding on review time, agree before the pilot starts what you'll do if your measure doesn't move.
